title: anchor-sunset-customer-transition-workbook
content:
Purpose
---
This is a practical, customer-centric workbook for sunsetting regional "anchors" (our term for tenant-anchored region pins) and migrating affected customers to the new unified residency model with graceful degradation paths. Audience: SRE, solutions engineering, account teams, legal, and customer success.

High-level goals
- Avoid dropped SLAs or data locality regressions for paying customers.
- Provide clear operator steps for migration and rollback.
- Ensure audit evidence for compliance customers during transition.
- Minimize developer lift for customers that accept automated migration.

Scope and non-goals
- Scope: customers currently using tenant region anchors (hard pins) that we plan to deprecate over the next 12 months. Includes hosted and dedicated tiers.
- Non-goal: this doc does not design the universal routing engine (separate RFC). Focus here is migration, comms, and runbook.

Key assumptions
- New unified residency model (URN) supports equivalent residency guarantees for 95% of anchor use-cases. Edge-only anchors (transient edge caches) out of scope for this wave.
- Customers will be offered: 1) auto-migrate (recommended), 2) assisted migration (SE plan + migration window), or 3) extended-pin for Ee customers (contracted).

Owner and escalation
- Primary owner: Maya Singh (eng-private-deployments)
- Ops lead during windows: Luca Romero (SRE)
- Legal/compliance contact: Priya Desai
- Escalation path: oncall -> SRE runbook -> Eng PM -> Head of Platform. Pager: #region-ops pager oncall.

Checklist (pre-migration: discovery & risk)
- [ ] Run customer impact query: list tenants with region_pin != null and last-90d traffic > 1000 requests/day. (Linear: PD-1327)
- [ ] Tag contractual constraints: attachments that require physical residency (eg: EU‑only KMS). Flag for Legal review.
- [ ] Telemetry baseline: capture latency, region-routed percentage, SLO violations, token volume per tenant for baseline week.
- [ ] Data flows inventory: store list of connectors that reference pinned storage endpoints (S3 buckets, KMS key locations).
- [ ] Risk score per tenant: combine traffic, contractual lock, support tier, and infra complexity (scale 1–5).

Customer migration paths (decision matrix)
- Auto-migrate: for low-risk tenants (score 1) with no contractual residency clause. System migrates during off-peak with validation checks and post-change monitoring.
- Assisted migration: for mid risk (score 2–3). SE + customer schedule a migration window; tech lead executes migration steps; runbook validated with customer tests.
- Contracted extension: for high risk (score 4–5) or customers with legal residency clauses; negotiate extended-pin or custom private deployment.

Pre-migration technical checklist (SE/SRE)
- [ ] Confirm model/version parity between anchor and URN fallback (model artifacts reproducible).
- [ ] Validate KMS/HSM key policies: URN access pattern must respect customer key scoping. If not, escalate to Security.
- [ ] Storage mapping: verify object-key rewrite rules for pinned buckets. Document mapping script (see section: object-rewrite-scripts).
- [ ] Create migration feature flag: migration.<tenant_id>.anchor-sunset. This allows immediate rollback toggling.
- [ ] Canary plan: pick 3 internal test tenants + 1 customer pilot. Run canary for 48 hours with real traffic.

Operator runbook (auto-migrate flow)
1) Pre-window: ensure maintenance window assigned and customer notified 72h in advance.
2) Snapshot telemetry baseline: run telemetry/exports for past 7 days (latency, error-rate, region tag).
3) Flip feature flag to staging for tenant; run synthetic validation (prompt set with expected deterministic responses).
4) Migrate routing: update tenant routing tag in DB from region_anchor -> urn_region_preference and propagate to router.
5) Monitor: intensive monitoring for 2 hours (SRE dashboard: tenant-level errors, fallbacks, region-drift). If errors spike > 2x baseline or privacy guard triggers, rollback.
6) Post-validation: set migration.<tenant>.completed=true, record audit evidence (signed JSON blob) and draft customer note.

Rollback criteria and steps
- Immediate rollback if: error rate > 2x baseline sustained for 15 minutes, privacy-capture event triggered, or customer reports data locality violation.
- Rollback steps: toggle migration feature flag back, revert routing DB change, invalidate caches and KV prefixes if applicable, re-run telemetry baseline. Escalate to eng: reason + traces attached.

Telemetry and audit evidence (must capture and store)
- Events to emit per-migration: migration.requested, migration.started, migration.completed, migration.rollback, migration.error. Each event must include: tenant_id, operator_id, timestamp, previous_anchor, new_urn_tag, git-sha of deployment, and snapshot pointers.
- Required artifacts: routing-config-diff (git), request-trace-sample (x10), S3-access-logs sample for affected buckets, KMS-policy-dump if keys touched.
- Storage: push to archived-migrations/tenant-id/YYYYMMDD.tar.gz with retention 2y for audit customers.

Legal & contract checks (SE checklist)
- Confirm there is no explicit 'data must not leave COUNTRY' clause. If clause exists, consult Priya and escalate.
- Capture acceptance: for EU‑UK cross-border cases ask customer to sign migration acknowledgement (template below). For regulated customers, ensure audit bundle is prepared before migration.

Customer communication templates (short form)
- Email subject: Important: upcoming improvement for region pinning (action recommended)
- Body (short): Hi <Name>, we’re consolidating regional pinning to our new residency model to improve availability and reduce cost. We propose migrating your tenant during the window <date>. Expected impact: near-zero downtime; validation tests required. If you have residency constraints please reply by <date>. SE contact: <name>.
- Acceptance reply template: "I acknowledge and accept migration on <date>"

Operator checklist (post-migration validation)
- [ ] Confirm tenant requests are routed to expected region >= 98% for first 24 hours (metric: tenant.region_affinity_pct).
- [ ] Check egress data paths: storage writes should hit mapped bucket locations (compare object-rewrite logs).
- [ ] KMS: confirm no unauthorized key use. Verify CloudKMS logs for new access patterns.
- [ ] Customer functional test: run customer-provided test suite or agreed prompt set.
- [ ] Sign-off email sent and copy stored in migration bundle.

Sample migration audit note (to be stored in bundle)
- timestamp: 2025-02-12T03:22Z
- operator: luca.romero@redwood.com
- tenant: tenant-1221
- action: auto-migrate anchor -> urn
- result: completed; 0.4% increase in 95p latency for first hour; no privacy flags.

Object-rewrite scripts (ops note)
- Lightweight python snippet to rewrite object base paths when moving from pinned buckets to URN logical buckets. Keep idempotent, log mapping pairs, and include checksums to validate integrity. Script location: github PR link in linked artifacts.

Testing plan and canary metrics (pass/fail criteria)
- Canary duration: 48 hours with at least 10k requests total and representative token distribution.
- Pass criteria: error-rate <= baseline+0.5pp, 95p latency <= baseline+10%, region-affinity >= 98%, no KMS denials.
- If canary fails, capture failure template and schedule root cause analysis.

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress)
- [ ] How to handle tenants with split storage (EU S3 + US analytics S3) where analytics must remain US-only? Proposal: keep analytics connectors pinned; migrate API path. Need SE design.
- [ ] Billing alignment for customers that paid for explicit anchor SLA: do we rebate, credit, or extend other benefits? Finance to advise.
- [ ] Automate migration bundle creation in infra-tools. Currently manual and error-prone.

Appendix A — customer acknowledgement template
"By replying YES to this email you acknowledge Redwood Inference will migrate your tenant routing from a tenant-specific region anchor to the new Residency Routing Namespace (URN). You confirm there are no contractual clauses preventing this change and accept the planned maintenance window. If you require a legal review, reply ATTACH_LEGAL and we will pause migration and engage the legal team."

Appendix B — quick-run troubleshooting snippets
- Check routing tag: SELECT region_anchor, urn_preference FROM tenants WHERE id = <tenant>
- Revert flag: curl -X POST https://internal-api/flags/migration.<tenant>.anchor-sunset/false -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
- Fetch recent traces: curl 'https://traces.internal/tenant/<tenant>?from=-1h'

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep migration windows during low traffic for each customer; we should batch small customers into 1–2 weekly waves to reduce toil.
- Coordinate with Billing: some customers may see small cost delta; prepare FAQs.

Attachments to create before first pilot
- migration-checklist-template.md
- migration-audit-bundle-template.json
- customer-ack-email-template.txt
- migration-flagging-service-runbook.md

Last edits
- 2025-02-12: added audit event schema and sample operator rollback steps (Maya).
- 2024-12-02: initial draft and discovery query (Luca).

End of workbook.
